Findings: two blocking C1(a) false negatives (CJK prose numbers never matched; any square-bracketed number exempt, not only [PENDING…]) and four minor detector weaknesses.

findings.title: C1(a) number gate is blind to numbers in Chinese prose (\w lookbehind matches CJK)
findings.what_goes_wrong: METRIC_RE uses `(?<![\w.])` and `(?![\w])`. In Python 3 str regexes \w matches CJK characters, so in unspaced Chinese prose a metric number adjacent to a Han character is never matched: '灵敏度为91.5%，AUC为0.912。' yields no metric numbers and '样本量n=412例' yields none. A fabricated untraced number in a zh draft passes the gate with exit 0.
findings.why_vulnerable: SKILL.md declares the skill serves papers 'in English or Chinese' and ships assets/paper_scaffold_zh.md, so zh drafts are an in-scope input. C1(a) says any metric-like number absent from the ledger must exit 1. The test fixture is English only, so nothing exercises this.
findings.how_to_confirm: Replicated METRIC_RE (copied verbatim, not project code) in python3 -I: finditer over '灵敏度为91.5%，AUC为0.912。' and '样本量n=412例' returns []. End-to-end: add a zh paragraph '灵敏度为93.2%。' to CLEAN_DRAFT with no ledger row and run check_paper.main -> expected exit 1, actual exit 0 (inference from the regex; not executed against the repo).
findings.recommendation: Use ASCII-only guards, e.g. `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_.])` / `(?![A-Za-z0-9_])` (or re.ASCII for the guard classes), also accept full-width ％ and ＝, and add a zh-prose test for untraced decimal, percentage and n= count.

findings.title: C1(a) every square-bracketed number is exempt, not just [PENDING…] flags
findings.what_goes_wrong: The first _STRIP_INLINE pattern `\[[^\]]*\]` deletes all bracketed text before metric matching. Square-bracket confidence intervals are standard in medical/imaging writing ('Dice 0.847 [95% CI 0.71, 0.80]'); the 95%, 0.71 and 0.80 are never checked against the ledger, so a fabricated CI passes with exit 0. Same for markdown link text '[AUC 0.93](fig.png)' and any '[0.93]'.
findings.why_vulnerable: C1(a) exempts a number only when it is 'inside a [PENDING…] flag'. The stripping is a broader exemption than the criterion allows, and the only test (test_pending_flag_headings_and_references_are_not_numbers) checks the permissive side, never that a non-PENDING bracketed number still fails.
findings.how_to_confirm: Replicated the strip + METRIC_RE in python3 -I on 'Dice 0.847 [95% CI 0.71, 0.80]': only '0.847' is found. End-to-end: change the fixture's '(95% CI 0.82-0.87)' to '[95% CI 0.71-0.80]' with the ledger unchanged; expected exit 1 naming 0.71, actual exit 0 (inference).
findings.recommendation: Strip only citation brackets (`\[[^\]]*@[^\]]*\]`) and disclosed flags (`\[(?:PENDING|UNVERIFIED)[^\]]*\]`); keep link targets stripped but scan link text. Add a test that a bracketed untraced CI fails.

findings.title: Disclosure downgrade guard untested: --allow-disclosed-flags could silence fake DOIs/xxx
findings.what_goes_wrong: Mutating `allow_flags and DISCLOSED_FLAG_RE.match(hit)` to `allow_flags` downgrades every placeholder (10.xxxx, xxx, [TBD]) to WARN when --allow-disclosed-flags is passed, and the suite stays green.
findings.why_vulnerable: test_fake_doi_placeholder_fails runs without the flag; test_pending_flag_fails_unless_disclosed only uses a [PENDING] hit. No test combines the flag with a non-disclosable placeholder, so C1(c) under the documented flag is undetected.
findings.how_to_confirm: Apply the mutant and run research-paper tests: all pass (inference from reading the tests).
findings.recommendation: Add a test: draft with both '[PENDING: x]' and 'doi:10.xxxx/abc', run with --allow-disclosed-flags, expect exit 1 with FAIL [placeholder] for the DOI and WARN for PENDING.

findings.title: Ledger values with thousands separators are split into fragments (false FAIL) and comma normalization is untested
findings.what_goes_wrong: ledger_numbers tokenizes with NUMBER_RE `\d+(?:\.\d+)?`, so a ledger value '1,204' becomes {'1','204'} while the draft 'n=1,204' normalizes to '1204' and is reported as untraced. Conversely, no test proves that a correctly ledgered comma count passes, so a mutant removing `.replace(",", "")` in normalize_number survives.
findings.why_vulnerable: This fails safe, but it produces false FAILs on correctly ledgered counts, and normalize_number's comma handling has no test pinning it.
findings.recommendation: Use `\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?` for ledger tokens and add a test with ledger '1,204' / draft 'n=1,204' expecting exit 0.

findings.title: Checklist gate: unchecked-box branch, TBD values and missing-cell rows are unpinned
findings.what_goes_wrong: Deleting the `- [ ]` branch (92-95) or emptying UNDISPOSED except "" leaves the suite green. A row with the disposition cell omitted entirely ('| 3. Data sources |') splits into one cell, fails `len(cells) >= 2` and is silently accepted.
findings.why_vulnerable: Only one checklist test exists (empty second cell). C1(d) is about an empty disposition column; an omitted cell is the same defect in a different shape.
findings.how_to_confirm: Read: '| 3. Data sources |'.strip('|').split('|') -> one cell -> skipped. Mutant on lines 92-95 not killed by any test.
findings.recommendation: Treat a table row (after the header) with fewer than 2 cells as undisposed; add tests for '- [ ] item', '| item | TBD |' and '| item |'.

findings.title: References-section exclusion not exercised although a test name claims it
findings.what_goes_wrong: The fixture's references line contains no decimal/percent after DOI stripping, so a mutant that never sets in_refs (integrity_gate.py:57-59) survives every test, despite test_pending_flag_headings_and_references_are_not_numbers naming references.
findings.why_vulnerable: Detector passes without exercising the behavior it names.
findings.how_to_confirm: Mutate split_body so in_refs stays False; reference line 'Smith J. ... 2024;310(2):1-12. doi:10.1148/...' produces no metric numbers and no citekeys, so all tests pass (inference).
findings.recommendation: Add a reference line with e.g. 'Vol 3.2, 45% ' and an '@key' inside References and assert exit 0 / no number-not-in-ledger.
